clue.text: Leave secretively from Embankment, quietly crossing City area

indicators.note: the embankment-plus-quiet piece crosses over, so straddles, the City area placed within it

parts.note: a dam is an embankment holding back water
EC, East Central, is the postal district of the City of London
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone slips away unnoticed from the Thames Embankment, tiptoeing across the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embankment' suggests the Thames riverside in London; it is just a barrier. The City is London's financial district, whose postcode prefix is East Central.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly or furtively, often to avoid notice.

clue.text: Expert pinching final article is accused

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing hold of, so the expert's word encloses the rest

parts.note: deft means skilful, expert
end means final part
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A skilled thief steals the last item and is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: The defendant is the person accused in a court case.

clue.text: Headgear worn by peer or individual in court

indicators.note: the words before it go inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: taken as written
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A nobleman or someone else wears a ceremonial hat in a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by peers on state occasions.

clue.text: Filthy place at end of road with poor visibility

indicators.note: the filthy place is set at the end of, after, the road

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
a sty is a pigsty, a filthy place

explanation.surface: A pigsty at the end of a road is hard to see in the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway from London to the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Misty weather is hazy, so visibility is poor.

clue.text: Forcefully put one's foot down before oriental flight

parts.note: stamped means brought one's foot down hard
E for eastern, oriental

explanation.surface: Someone puts their foot down hard just before boarding a flight to the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' looks like air travel; here it is a panicked rush to flee, and 'Forcefully put one's foot down' is a past tense, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of frightened animals or people, a flight in panic.

clue.text: Old Harry's address? And here he is!

definitions.text: Old Harry's address? And here he is!

parts.words: Old Harry's address? And here he is!
parts.note: Old Harry is a nickname for Satan, so his address is a speech by him; the exclamation recalls the saying used when someone just mentioned turns up

explanation.definitionFit: The saying is used when a person who was being discussed appears, and literally means speech by Satan.

clue.text: Treat badly George Frederick's daughter, say

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the phrase and listen to it

parts.note: the composer George Frederick Handel; a daughter of his would be Miss Handel

explanation.surface: The composer's daughter is said to have been treated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Handel never married, which adds to the absurdity.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishandle someone is to treat them roughly or wrongly.

clue.text: Mournful English present left mostly about one

indicators.note: the shortened gift goes round, about, the letter for one
mostly means all but the final letter of the word

parts.note: a legacy is a gift left in a will
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An English bequest leaves someone feeling sorrowful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LEGACY to LEGAC, and 'about' wraps that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means having the sad tone of a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Provide proper directions for a start

indicators.note: the directions are placed at the start, before the word for proper

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
due means fitting, proper

explanation.surface: Someone is given the right route to begin a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is an old verb meaning to endow or supply someone with a quality.

clue.text: Decide it's lipstick, say, on new denims

parts.note: lipstick is an example of make-up
taken as written

indicators.note: new means made over afresh, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone concludes it is lipstick smeared on their new jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DENIMS into ESMIND; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a firm decision is the idiom's meaning: settle one's choice.

clue.text: Prevent a couple of new drivers landing on trees

indicators.note: in an across answer the drivers come to rest after, so on, the trees

parts.note: a forest is a mass of trees
L is the learner plate on a new driver's car; a couple gives two of them

explanation.surface: Two learner drivers crash-land in a wood, which someone might have hoped to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain new drivers display an L plate, so L stands for a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in advance to stop something happening.

clue.text: Bring success to expedition

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is an old sense meaning to make them prosper, as in 'God ...'
expedition in its old sense of promptness or haste

explanation.definitionFit: Speed once meant prosper or cause to prosper, and expedition also means swiftness of action.

clue.text: Overprotect the kids' mother

definitions.meaning: to fuss over someone too protectively, coddle
kids are young goats, and their mother is a female goat

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to mollycoddle, and a she-goat, mother of kids, has the same name.

clue.text: Reminiscent of Morse's last case

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word Morse alone

parts.note: the vocative is a grammatical case used in addressing someone

explanation.surface: The final investigation of Inspector Morse brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse's last case' suggests the TV detective; really it is the last letter of Morse plus a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative calls up memories or feelings, so it is reminiscent of them.

clue.text: Foresaw opposing head being taken in by detectives

parts.note: anti means against, opposing

indicators.note: the head is held inside, taken in by, the detectives

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Someone foresaw that a rival leader would be arrested by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To have anticipated something is to have expected or predicted it in advance.

clue.text: Red colouring of carbonaceous rock spread over ridge

indicators.note: the rock is spread over, so encloses, the ridge

parts.note: coal is a carbon-rich rock
a chine is a mountain ridge

explanation.surface: A red stain on a coal seam runs along a mountain crest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a scarlet dye from crushed insects, used to colour food.

clue.text: Source of corn required for horse

definitions.meaning: the central cylinder of a maize ear that bears the kernels

explanation.definitionFit: A corn cob holds the kernels, and a cob is also a stocky breed of horse.

clue.text: Warder — one grumbling about 'ot weather?

indicators.note: the grumbler goes round, about, the dropped-aitch weather

parts.note: to beef is to complain, so a beefer grumbles
heat, with the H dropped as the apostrophe in 'ot shows

explanation.surface: A guard moans about the sweltering heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders of the Tower of London; the dropped H of 'ot signals 'EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeater is the popular name for a Yeoman Warder guarding the Tower of London.

clue.text: Milk on this is regularly available

definitions.meaning: to milk a resource is to draw on it or exploit it
a thing 'on' a valve or spigot is readily available, the idiom for a ready supply

explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a source is to tap it, and something always to hand is said to be on tap.

clue.text: Knight errant's power over a youth at home

indicators.note: in a down answer the letter for power sits over, above, the rest

parts.note: P is the symbol for power
a lad is a youth
in means at home

explanation.surface: A wandering knight holds sway over a boy who stays at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin is a chivalrous champion, one of Charlemagne's peers, a roving knight.

clue.text: Accomplice of crook freed at once

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or wrong, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A criminal's partner was released at the same moment as him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like the criminal; it is the anagram signal, and 'of' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A confederate is an ally or partner in some shady scheme.

clue.text: A pound added to money earlier than 14

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra
the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: An extra pound is added to the cash beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: '14' points to the answer at 14 across; the definition reads 'earlier than' that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Done sooner than expected is the sense, before the predicted time.

clue.text: Everything I concealed in old fashioned mattress

indicators.note: the first words are hidden away inside the old-fashioned word

parts.note: passé means out of date, old-fashioned
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone stuffed all their valuables inside an antique mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: A palliasse is a straw-filled mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A palliasse is a thin mattress stuffed with straw.

clue.text: Through which we see a child in a stream

definitions.meaning: the dark opening in the eye that admits light
a schoolchild placed in an ability group, a stream

explanation.definitionFit: The eye's aperture and a schoolchild share the name; British schools sort children into streams by ability.

clue.text: It sounds like swell material

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the word for swell is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a surge is a swell of the sea

explanation.surface: A fabric is described as sounding marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like an adjective, great; it is a noun, a rising of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth.

clue.text: One may be fired, covering for a nut

definitions.meaning: an artillery projectile shot from a gun
the hard outer case of a nut

explanation.definitionFit: An artillery round and the hard casing of a nut both go by this name.

clue.text: Serviceman requiring a doctor during exercise

indicators.note: the doctor comes in the middle of, during, the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A soldier needs medical attention in the middle of a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a military chaplain, a member of the armed services.

clue.text: Like travellers, one can rave about the East

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tin is a can
E is the abbreviation for east
to rant is to rave

explanation.surface: Travelling folk, one finds, tend to go on about the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' merely sets the ranting beside the East, which comes just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant describes those who travel from place to place, as nomads or wandering workers do.

clue.text: It's her job to supply the board with accommodation

definitions.text: It's her job to supply the board with accommodation

parts.words: It's her job to supply the board with accommodation
parts.note: the surface suggests a firm housing its directors; board means meals, as in board and lodging, offered by a woman who lets rooms

explanation.definitionFit: A woman who runs a lodging house provides lodgers with meals and a room.

clue.text: Musical performer better on piano

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece set on another comes after it, so the better follows the piano

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
one who bets, a layer of odds

explanation.surface: A musician who plays the piano rather better than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like 'superior'; it is one who bets, a layer of odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs on a musical instrument.
